title: Curved momentum space and finite Landau spectrum in $κ$-Minkowski spacetime
abstract: It is obtained the $κ$-Poincare Casimir from the de Sitter geometry of momentum space and employed as the dynamical constraint governing charged particles within the framework of Poisson gauge theory. The resulting formalism is applied to investigate both scalar and spin-1/2 particles in a constant magnetic field. Exact energy spectra are obtained, including all orders in the deformation parameter $1/κ$. The curvature of momentum space implies a maximal invariant momentum, which in turn leads to a finite Landau spectrum characterized by the existence of a Highest Landau Level (HLL). In the fermionic case, the truncation becomes spin dependent, resulting in a polarized HLL. Possible implications of this ultraviolet truncation and its relation to anomaly-related phenomena are briefly discussed.
summary: This paper analyzes particle motion in $\kappa$-Minkowski spacetime, treating momentum space as curved de Sitter geometry. By using a deformed Casimir invariant, they derive exact energy spectra for charged particles in a magnetic field. The key finding is that the curvature imposes a maximal momentum, resulting in a finite Landau spectrum with a Highest Landau Level.
main_problem: The research investigates particle dynamics in $\kappa$-Minkowski spacetime, linking the geometry of curved momentum space to physical observables like energy spectra.
main_result: The curvature imposes a fundamental upper bound on invariant momentum, leading to a finite Landau spectrum characterized by a Highest Landau Level (HLL).
method: The authors employ Poisson gauge theory and geometric methods, deriving the $\kappa$-Poincaré Casimir operator from de Sitter geometry.
model_or_system: The model considers charged scalar and spin-1/2 particles moving in a constant magnetic field within the framework of non-commutative $\kappa$-Minkowski spacetime.
key_observables: Exact energy spectra, Highest Landau Level (HLL), and the deformed Dirac equation constraint.
important_parameters: The deformation parameter $\kappa$ acts as an ultraviolet cutoff scale; the magnetic field strength $B$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing gauge-invariant dynamics using Poisson brackets, and specific choices for operator ordering are noted in the quantization process.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the energy $E(|\vec{p}|)$ versus $|\vec{p}|$ for different regimes, showing the transition from commutative to $\kappa$-Minkowski energies up to the boundary $|\vec{p}| = \kappa$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the formalism by first establishing the geometric structure of momentum space via the Casimir invariant ($C_\kappa$), then applying this framework to derive gauge-invariant equations of motion for scalar and spin-1/2 particles, culminating in the calculation of the finite Landau spectrum.
why_interesting: While focused on high-energy spacetime physics, the concept of a fundamental UV cutoff leading to discrete, bounded spectra (like the HLL) has parallels in effective field theories or condensed matter systems where confinement or quantization occurs at an intrinsic scale.
